name: claude-kit
check_batch: `npm run check`, and `npm test` after a change under `bin/`, read for the change just made and nothing else
check_once: `npm run sync`, then `npm run kit:check` in each plugin repo
not_for: Not for a file a plugin repo owns (its `AGENTS.md`, `repo-*` rules and skills, `repo.json`), which is changed in that repo.
settled: A design already settled by the user's rulings skips the spec and goes to the plan.
checks: - per batch: `npm run check`, read for the change just made and nothing else;
- after a change under `bin/`: `npm test`, with a test added or changed for the behaviour that moved;
- once: `npm run sync`, then `npm run kit:check` in each plugin repo.
voice: single dashes, single quotes in prose
commit: its message in the form the log already has (`type(scope): what is now true`), with no trace of the agent (`.claude/rules/commits.md`)
not_here: - A change to a plugin repo's own files, which follows that repo's own flow; this repo only syncs the shared ones into it.
- Alfred Code's `task-solve` and its seats, stamps and stops, which serve the projects that install the stack.
structure_map: - `bin/` is flat by contract: the sync copies a named list of its files into each repo's `.claude/kit/` (`KIT_FILES` in `bin/sync.ts`), so a feature here is a file, not a folder.

- Entries, each run with `node`: `bin/sync.ts`, `bin/check.mjs`, `bin/settings.mjs`, `bin/status-hook.mjs`. Logic two of them share is a module of exported functions beside them (`bin/kit-settings.mjs`) that takes what it reads as arguments (`env`, `root`).
- The outside world: `node:fs`, `node:child_process`, `process.env`, stdin and stdout, the clock.

- Named values live in `bin/constants.mjs`, copied with the scripts that import it (`KIT_FILES`); a new one goes there. The constants still at the top of `bin/sync.ts` and `bin/check.mjs` move there when a change adds or rewrites one.
- Tests: `test/<script>.test.mjs`, run against throwaway kits and repos (`test/support.mjs`).

notes: shared/skills is the one home: bin/sync.ts copies each skill into .claude/skills of this repo and of alfred-code, alfred-mods and alfred-tools. No plugin install carries them, so there is no manifest, catalog or eval suite - the tested surface is the sync and each repo's kit:check.

A file ending in .tmpl (solve-task/SKILL.md.tmpl) is a template: audit its text with the {{key}} slots as written, and the filled copy at .claude/skills/solve-task/SKILL.md for what a session reads. A slot's value is each repo's own, in its .claude/kit/repo.json.

The eight repo-audit-* skills carry disable-model-invocation: their descriptions are not in context, so the trigger grade judges the slash-menu line, not model triggering. repo-audit-flow is the opposite - hidden from the slash menu, loaded by those eight. Every other skill is model-invocable.

The authoring method is this repo's own skill-authoring skill: a description of at most 160 characters on one line, opening on its trigger. The skills name each other freely because the whole set is always synced together.

javascript, typescript, ts-js-testing, npm, markdown-style and code-comments began as copies of Alfred Code stack skills and have diverged; alfred-code's stack/skills copies are that repo's product and are not kept in step from here.
A fix lands under shared/skills, never in a .claude/ copy; after it, npm run sync and one commit in each of the three repos.
No usage ledger exists for these skills.

The multi-home registry is copies.json at the kit's root: the auto-run, refining-plans and typescript SKILL.md files own text their rules repeat on purpose, the refining-plans reviewer prompt owns the contract the plan-grader agent repeats, and repo-audit-skills and repo-audit-rules own the six blocks the audit family shares - each pinned by marker phrases. A pass that rewords such text updates the copies and the registry in the same pass; `node .claude/kit/check.mjs` fails here when a site lacks one of its markers, and when a skill's description is not one line of at most 160 characters.

Three agents, each a template whose model line is a {{key}} filled from shared/defaults.json: audit-planner (plan_model, opus), audit-editor (implement_model, sonnet), plan-grader (review_model, opus). A project changes a role's model through KIT_PLAN_MODEL, KIT_REVIEW_MODEL or KIT_IMPLEMENT_MODEL in its settings, which bin/kit-settings.mjs resolves and the dispatching skill passes. The filled copies are under .claude/agents/.

audit-planner and audit-editor are dispatched only by the repo-audit-flow skill: the planner reads, scores and writes the edit plan and never edits an audited file; the editor applies the plan and decides nothing. That split of tools is by design.

plan-grader is meant to be dispatched only by the refining-plans skill. The skill does not dispatch it yet: it still sends a general-purpose reviewer with references/reviewer-prompt.md until the two are compared on one sample (state on 2026-11-15).
An agent definition loads at session start, so a new or changed one needs a restart before it can be dispatched.

Rules without a paths field load in every session of all four repos: auto-run, commits, execution, plan-approval, refining-plans, superpowers-location. execution.md.tmpl is a template whose check_batch and check_once come from each repo's repo.json. The path-scoped ones - javascript, typescript, skill-authoring, project-structure - each exist to load their skill; project-structure.md.tmpl is a template whose paths are each repo's structure_paths.
No always-on budget is enforced here; alfred-code's lint budget covers its stack rules, not these.
The instruction file every rule sits beside is AGENTS.md at each repo's root, never a CLAUDE.md.

The multi-home registry is copies.json at the kit's root: each text kept on purpose in more than one file - a rule and its skill, a rule and each repo's AGENTS.md, the load contract the path-scoped rules share - with its owner, every copy and the marker phrases each site keeps. A pass that adds, moves or rewords such text updates it in the same pass; `node .claude/kit/check.mjs` fails here when a site lacks one of its markers.
This repo ships no instruction template: AGENTS.md is its own instruction file and is the audit target. There is no installer, seed or fill skill.
Claude Code reads it only while no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists; check.mjs fails when one does.
README.md holds the mechanism in full - the shared paths, the templates, the audit map. AGENTS.md is the hub and points at it instead of repeating it.

The multi-home registry is copies.json at the kit's root: AGENTS.md here and in each plugin repo keeps a registered copy of the commits rule, pinned by marker phrases. A pass that rewords it keeps those markers, or changes the owner rule and the registry with it in the same pass; `node .claude/kit/check.mjs` fails here when a site lacks one of its markers.

One hook, by the user's request of 2026-11-15, which replaced that morning's no-hook decision: bin/status-hook.mjs, a UserPromptSubmit command hook wired in shared/settings.base.json and merged into each repo's .claude/settings.json by bin/sync.ts, which recognises a kit hook by the .claude/kit/ path in its command. It shows one status line to the user and the same values to Claude, saves in .claude/kit/settings.json a request whose first line is only words to switch auto-run or scoring or to name a role's model ('plan model fable'), where it holds until it is changed, and never blocks a request; test/status-hook.test.mjs and test/status-hook-models.test.mjs cover it. Any other hook still waits for a rule that is seen to fail. The audit also covers the hooks that enabled plugins bring into a session here: the plugins in .claude/settings.json enabledPlugins and those enabled at user scope.
